Techniques for winning battles on the map.
<C=7>Unit Movement</C># A unit's Movement is the average of# its machines' Movement, so raising# each machine's raises the unit's.

<C=7>Spirit Commands</C># Using the Spirit Command <C=7>Accel</C> gives# a unit +3 Movement.## When forming Twin Units, we recommend# putting a machine with Accel in# each Twin Unit.##  <C=7>Accel</C>  Movement +3

<C=7>Parts</C># Equipping Parts raises a machine's# Movement. Other Parts besides the two# below also raise Movement. When you# get one, try equipping it on a machine# that needs more Movement.##  <C=7>Booster</C>      Movement +1##  <C=7>Megabooster</C>  Movement +2

<C=7>Unit Movement Type</C># A unit's movement type changes how much# Movement it spends crossing terrain.# Movement type combines "Air," "Land,"# and "Water." Text color shows aptitude:# white is best, then gray, then none.## Crossing poor terrain costs more# Movement than usual.## A unit's movement type depends on the# types of its machines, and each# machine's type can be changed by# equipping Parts.##  <C=7>Dustproofer</C>  Gain movement type Land##  <C=7>Water Jet</C>    Gain movement type Water

Dealing heavy damage to shoot down foes#is the basis of winning battles. Common#ways to deal heavy damage include:##  <C=7>Spirit Commands</C>#  <C=7>Pilot Training</C>#  <C=7>Weapon Upgrades</C>#  <C=7>Weapon Choice</C>#  <C=7>Will</C>#  <C=7>Attack Methods</C>

<C=7>Spirit Commands</C># Some Spirit and Twin Spirit Commands# raise damage directly, and others help# you deal damage effectively. Here are# some typical ones:##  <C=7>Valor</C>    Doubles damage dealt#           for one attack##  <C=7>Pierce</C>   Nullifies the target's#           defensive skills##  <C=7>Mettle</C>   All attacks are critical#           for 1 turn#           Doesn't stack with Valor/Soul##  <C=7>Soul</C>     Damage dealt x2.5 for#           one attack

<C=7>Pilot Training</C># Raising a pilot's Melee and Ranged# stats increases the damage dealt by# melee and ranged weapons respectively.# Each stat point basically raises# damage dealt by 0.5%# (more or less due to other factors).## Learning combat-related Skills can# also raise damage dealt in certain# situations. Here are some typical ones:##  <C=7>In-Fighter</C>  Higher skill levels#              raise melee weapon power#              (or Movement)##  <C=7>Gunfighter</C>  Higher skill levels#              raise ranged weapon power#              (or range)##  <C=7>Attacker</C>    Activates at Will 130+;#              final damage dealt#              is multiplied by 1.2##  <C=7>Revenge</C>     When counterattacking,#              final damage dealt x1.2##  <C=7>Cooperative Attack</C>#              Support Attacks (normally#              75% damage) deal the same#              damage as normal attacks##  <C=7>Focused Attack</C>  When a main (sub)#              unit attacks a sub (main)#              unit, the damage penalty#              (-35%) is offset by 20%## <C=7>Stat Increases and Learning Skills</C># are done via <C=7>Pilot Training</C> in the# Intermission. Training requires PP,# earned in battles on the map.
strings.retry_note: "<C=7>Pilot Training</C># Raising a pilot's Melee and Ranged# stats boosts damage from melee and# ranged weapons respectively. Each point# raises damage by about 0.5% (varies# with other factors).## Learning combat-related Skills can# also raise damage in certain# situations. Here are some typical ones:##  <C=7>In-Fighter</C>  Higher skill levels#              raise melee weapon power#              (or Movement)##  <C=7>Gunfighter</C>  Higher skill levels#              raise ranged weapon power#              (or range)##  <C=7>Attacker</C>    At Will 130+, final#              damage dealt x1.2##  <C=7>Revenge</C>     Final damage x1.2#              when countering##  <C=7>Cooperative Attack</C>#              Support attacks (normally#              75% damage) deal full#              damage##  <C=7>Focused Attack</C>#              Main (sub) vs. sub (main)#              attacks: damage penalty#              (-35%) improved by 20%## <C=7>Stat Increases</C> and <C=7>Learning Skills</C># are done via <C=7>Pilot Training</C> in# the Intermission. Training requires PP,# earned through battles on the map." failed: tags differ from the Japanese (18 vs 20)

strings.en: <C=7>Weapon Upgrades</C># Weapon Upgrades in the Intermission# raise weapons' attack power. Upgrades# cost money earned in map battles.##<C=7>Weapon Choice</C># Besides attack power, many factors# affect a weapon's damage. Choose your# weapons with their traits in mind.##  <C=7>Beam Weapons</C>  Watch for barriers#                that stop beams, or that#                stop all but beams##  <C=7>Barrier Pierce</C>  Ignores barriers#                  to deal damage## Each weapon's terrain rating shows the# terrain it's best in. Ratings go S, A,# B, C, D; S deals the most damage, so# we recommend picking weapons to suit# the terrain.## Final damage also varies with the# pilot's Melee and Ranged stats, so we# recommend melee weapons for pilots# good at melee, and ranged weapons for# pilots good at shooting.
<C=7>Will</C># Higher Will raises attack and defense.# Raise Will as much as you can before# attacking, and target enemies with low# Will.

<C=7>Attack Methods</C># Combining attack methods lets you deal# more damage. Here's a typical example:##  <C=7>Support Attack</C>  An adjacent unit#                  attacks after the#                  enemy counters.#                  Needs the Support#                  Attack skill##<C=7>Weakening the Enemy</C># Weapons with the <C=7>Armor Down</C> effect# lower the target's armor. Using them# before a strong attack is very# effective.

Weapons fall into 3 types by how many#targets they can attack.##  <C=7>Normal Weapons</C>#  <C=7>ALL Weapons</C>#  <C=7>MAP Weapons</C>##Weapons also have various individual#traits beyond their targets. Used well,#the <C=7>Special Effect Weapons</C> below#can be a big help in battle.##  <C=7>Special Effect Weapons</C>#  <C=7>Barrier Pierce Weapons</C>##Each entry explains their traits and#recommends how to use them.

<C=7>Normal Weapons<S=4><I=66><S=2></C># Weapons that target 1 enemy machine.# They can be combined with Support# Attacks, so we recommend them for# focusing damage on one machine.# When a Twin Unit attacks an enemy Twin# Unit, you can choose from these two# attack types:##  <C=7>Split Attack</C>#    Your two machines each attack a#    different machine of the enemy pair##  <C=7>Concentrated Attack</C>#    Your two machines both attack just#    one machine of the enemy pair

<C=7>ALL Weapons<S=4><I=66><S=-45><I=64><S=7></C># Weapons that hit every machine in the# target unit. Support Attacks can't join# them, but they're great for wiping out# an enemy Twin Unit in one go.# Main (sub) vs. main (sub) deals normal# damage, but main (sub) vs. sub (main)# damage is cut to <C=7>65%</C>.## With the <C=7>Focused Attack</C> skill, this# becomes <C=7>85%</C>.##<C=7>Double Attack Weapons<S=4><I=66><S=-45><I=65><S=7></C># Some ALL weapons can also hit units# adjacent to the target. They use twice# the EN and ammo, but adjacent units# can't counter, so use them freely.

<C=7>MAP Weapons<S=4><I=66><S=-45><I=63><S=7></C># Weapons that hit every unit inside each# weapon's set area, friend or foe alike.# Some MAP weapons, however, can# <C=7>tell friend from foe</C> and only damage# enemies in the area.## MAP weapons ignore the main-vs-sub# damage cut. Unlike normal attacks, the# enemy can't counter them. They do use# lots of EN or have little ammo, so save# them for good situations, like when# several enemies are grouped together.

<C=7>Special Effect Weapons</C># Weapons whose attribute on the weapon# screen shows <S=4><I=59><S=-52><I=60><S=38>.# On a hit, they inflict various effects# besides damage. Here are typical ones:##  <C=7>Mobility Down</C>  Lowers the target's#                 Mobility so attacks#                 hit more easily##  <C=7>Armor Down</C>     Lowers the target's#                 Armor so you can deal#                 more damage##<C=7>Barrier Pierce Weapons</C># Check for this trait in the list shown# by pressing <S=3><I=4><S=2> on the weapon screen.# Weapons with it ignore enemy barriers# when dealing damage.#
When damage drops a machine's HP to <C=1>0</C>,# it is shot down. Losing units weakens# your forces, and in some cases means# <C=1>Game Over</C>.

<C=7>Spirit Commands</C># Some Spirit Commands reduce the damage# you take. Here are some typical ones:##   <C=7>Persist</C>  Damage taken is 10 for#            one hit##   <C=7>Wall</C>     Damage taken is cut to#            1/4 for 1 turn##<C=7>Will</C># Higher Will raises attack and defense.# We recommend raising Will as much as# possible before enemies attack you.

<C=7>Pilot Training</C># Raising a pilot's <C=7>Defense</C> stat# reduces the damage taken from enemies.# Each point basically reduces damage# taken by 0.5%# (more or less due to other factors).## Learning defensive <C=7>Skills</C> can# also reduce damage taken in certain# situations. Here's a typical one:##   <C=7>Guard</C>   At Will 130+, final damage#           taken from enemies is 80%## <C=7>Stat Increases and Learning Skills</C># are done via <C=7>Pilot Training</C> in the# Intermission. Training requires PP,# earned in battles on the map.
strings.retry_note: "<C=7>Pilot Training</C># Raising a pilot's <C=7>Defense</C> stat reduces# damage taken from enemies. Each point# reduces damage taken by about 0.5%# (varies with other factors).## Learning defensive <C=7>Skills</C> can also# reduce damage taken in certain# situations. Here's a typical one:##   <C=7>Guard</C>   At Will 130+, final damage#           taken is 80%## <C=7>Stat Increases</C> and <C=7>Learning Skills</C># are done via <C=7>Pilot Training</C> in# the Intermission. Training requires PP,# earned through battles on the map." failed: tags differ from the Japanese (12 vs 14)

strings.en: <C=7>Terrain Ability</C># Damage taken also depends on a unit's# <C=7>Terrain Ability</C>, which is set by both# the <C=7>machine's</C> and the <C=7>pilot's</C>.# There are <C=7>5 grades</C>: S, A, B, C, D.# Higher grades give better defense, so# fight on favorable terrain when you can.##<C=7>Terrain Effects</C># Some terrain reduces damage from# enemies. To take less damage, we# recommend placing units on terrain that# raises defense. Note that flying units# don't get terrain effects.

<C=7>Unit Upgrades</C># Raising a machine's Armor with Unit# Upgrades in the Intermission reduces# damage taken. HP can also be raised# with Unit Upgrades. Upgrades cost money# earned in map battles.##<C=7>Parts</C># Equipping Parts raises a machine's# Armor and HP. Here are typical ones:##  <C=7>Chobham Armor</C>  Max HP +500#                 Armor +100##  <C=7>Hybrid Armor</C>   Max HP +1000#                 Armor +150##  <C=7>Orichalconium</C>  Max HP +1000#                 Armor +200

<C=7>Defensive Methods</C># Making good use of pilot skills and# unit abilities lets you reduce the# damage you take from enemies.# Here are some typical examples.##  <C=7>Shield Equipped</C>  Units with a shield#        take a further 10% less damage#        than normal units when they#        choose Defend.#        Whether a unit has a shield is#        shown by an icon on the unit#        status screen.##  <C=7>Support Defense</C>  An adjacent unit#        takes the enemy's damage in#        your place while defending.#        Needs the Support Defense skill.

Landing hits on the enemy is one of the#most important elements of combat.#Typical ways to raise your hit rate#include the following:##    <C=7>Spirit Commands</C>#    <C=7>Pilot Training</C>#    <C=7>Terrain Ability</C>#    <C=7>Enhancement Parts</C>#    <C=7>Target Size</C>#    <C=7>Distance to Target</C>#    <C=7>Attack Method</C>##Each section explains their features and#recommends how to use them.

<C=7>Spirit Commands</C># These Spirit Commands raise hit rate:##    <C=7>Bullseye</C>  For 1 turn,#            hit rate becomes 100%##    <C=7>Focus</C>  For 1 turn,#            hit and evasion rates +30%##<C=7>Pilot Training</C># Raising a pilot's <C=7>Accuracy</C> stat# raises the hit rate of your attacks.## You can also learn <C=7>Skills</C> that# raise hit rate.# Here is a typical one:##   <C=7>Predict</C>  At Will 130+, final hit#            and evasion rates +10%## <C=7>Stat Increases and Learning Skills</C># are done via <C=7>Pilot Training</C> in the# Intermission. Training requires PP,# earned in battles on the map.

<C=7>Terrain Ability</C># Hit rate also changes with a unit's# <C=7>Terrain Ability</C>, which is decided by# both <C=7>Unit Terrain Ability</C> and# <C=7>Pilot Terrain Ability</C>. It's judged by# the terrain the unit stands on, in# <C=7>5 ranks</C> (S, A, B, C, D). Higher ranks# give bigger bonuses, so fight on your# best terrain when possible.## <C=7>Pilot Terrain Ability</C> can be raised# via <C=7>Pilot Training</C> in the Intermission.# <C=7>Unit Terrain Ability</C> can be raised,# like <C=7>Movement Type</C>, by equipping# Enhancement Parts.

<C=7>Enhancement Parts</C># Equipping Enhancement Parts raises# weapon accuracy. Typical parts:##    <C=7>Dual Sensor</C>   Weapon hit rate +10%##    <C=7>Multi-Sensor</C>  Weapon hit rate +20%##<C=7>Target Size</C># The larger the target, the higher the# hit rate. There are <C=7>5 sizes</C>: LL, L, M,# S, SS, with bonuses decreasing from LL.
<C=7>Distance to Target</C># The closer you are to the target,# the higher your hit rate.
<C=7>Attack Method</C># With a Support Attack, the supporting# unit gets a <C=7>+20%</C> hit rate bonus.

Avoiding enemy attacks is one of the#most important elements of combat.#Typical ways to raise your evasion#include the following:##    <C=7>Spirit Commands</C>#    <C=7>Pilot Training</C>#    <C=7>Terrain Ability</C>#    <C=7>Unit Upgrades</C>#    <C=7>Enhancement Parts</C>#    <C=7>Terrain Effects</C>#    <C=7>Distance to Target</C>##Each section explains their features and#recommends how to use them.

<C=7>Spirit Commands</C># These Spirit Commands raise evasion:##    <C=7>Focus</C>  For 1 turn,#           hit and evasion rates +30%##    <C=7>Flash</C>  Evade all attacks for 1 battle##<C=7>Pilot Training</C># Raising a pilot's <C=7>Evasion</C> stat# raises evasion against enemy attacks.## You can also learn Skills that# raise evasion.# Here is a typical one:##   <C=7>Predict</C>  At Will 130+, final hit#            and evasion rates +10%## <C=7>Stat Increases and Learning Skills</C># are done via <C=7>Pilot Training</C> in the# Intermission. Training requires PP,# earned in battles on the map.

<C=7>Unit Upgrades</C># Raising a unit's <C=7>Mobility</C> via# <C=7>Unit Upgrades</C> in the Intermission# raises evasion against enemy attacks.# Upgrades require Funds, earned in# battles on the map.##<C=7>Enhancement Parts</C># Equipping Enhancement Parts raises a# unit's <C=7>Mobility</C>, and evasion with it.# Typical parts:##    <C=7>Servomotor</C>  Mobility  +5##    <C=7>Biosensor</C>   Mobility +20

<C=7>Terrain Effects</C># Some terrain raises evasion against# enemy attacks. When you want to dodge,# we recommend placing units on terrain# that boosts evasion.# Note that flying units don't receive# terrain effects.##<C=7>Terrain Ability</C># Evasion also changes with a unit's# <C=7>Terrain Ability</C>, which is decided by# both <C=7>Unit Terrain Ability</C> and# <C=7>Pilot Terrain Ability</C>. It's judged by# the terrain the unit stands on, in# <C=7>5 ranks</C> (S, A, B, C, D). Higher ranks# give bigger bonuses, so fight on your# best terrain when possible.##<C=7>Pilot Terrain Ability</C> can be raised#via <C=7>Pilot Training</C> in the Intermission.#<C=7>Unit Terrain Ability</C> can be raised,#like Movement Type, by equipping#<C=7>Enhancement Parts</C>.
<C=7>Distance to Target</C># The farther you are from the attacking# enemy, the higher your evasion.

Some special abilities of robots help#with defense. Here are typical ones:##    <C=7>Shield Equipped</C>#    <C=7>Barriers</C>#    <C=7>Afterimage</C>#    <C=7>Blocks</C>##Each section explains their features.

<C=7>Shield Equipped</C># The <C=7>Shield</C> icon on the unit status# screen shows whether a unit has this.# When such a unit chooses Defend against# an enemy attack, it takes 10% less# damage than a unit without a <C=7>Shield</C>.##<C=7>Barriers</C># These reduce or nullify enemy damage.# There are many types, each with its# own traits. Here are typical ones:##  - <C=7>Beam Coat</C>#    Reduces <C=7>ranged beam</C> damage by <C=7>900</C>#    Uses <C=7>5</C> EN when activated##  - <C=7>Gravity Territory</C>#    Nullifies damage of <C=7>1800</C> or less#    Uses <C=7>15</C> EN when activated##Barriers come in <C=7>reducing types</C> and#<C=7>nullifying types</C>. Reducing types lower#final damage; nullifying types reduce#damage to <C=7>0</C> if the attack is at or below#their value.##Some barriers can also be equipped#via Enhancement Parts.

<C=7>Afterimage</C># Has a <C=7>50%</C> chance to evade attacks.# Activates at Will <C=7>130</C>+.##<C=7>Blocks</C># Abilities that nullify special effects# of enemy attacks, with various Blocks# for each type of effect. Typical ones:##  - <C=7>Mind Block</C>#    Nullifies P-type special effects:#    <C=7>Will Down, SP Drain, Spirit Seal</C>##  - <C=7>Energy Block</C>#    Nullifies R-type special effects:#    <C=7>EN Down, EN Drain</C>

Some special abilities of robots#help with movement.#Here are typical ones:##<C=7>Transform</C>/<C=7>Combine</C>/<C=7>Replace</C>/<C=7>Separate</C># The ability to change form on the map.# This alters the unit's traits and may# change its Movement Type or Movement.

Pilot skills include ones that are:#    <C=7>Useful for attacking</C>#    <C=7>Useful for hitting and evading</C>#    <C=7>Useful for defending</C>#These skills can be learned through#<C=7>Pilot Training</C> in the Intermission.#Training requires PP, earned in#battles on the map.

<C=7>Support Attack</C># A skill that lets a unit join in after# an adjacent unit's attack.# Combat proceeds in this order:# <C=7>Attack</C>#    v# <C=7>Enemy Counter</C>#    v# <C=7>Support Attack</C># It can activate as many times per turn# as its skill level.##<C=7>Cooperative Attack</C># A skill used together with the# <C=7>Support Attack</C> skill.# When learned, Support Attacks (normally# 75% damage) deal the same damage as# normal attacks. Recommended for pilots# with a high Support Attack skill level.##<C=7>Focused Attack</C># When a main (sub) unit attacks a sub# (main) unit, the damage penalty (-35%)# is offset by 20%. Recommended for# pilots who often use ALL attacks.

<C=7>Predict</C>#  Activates at <C=7>130</C> Will or higher,#  raising final hit and evasion by 10%.#  As <C=7>+10% is added to the final rate</C>,#  when this skill activates, you're#  assured at least 10% vs. any enemy.##  Other skills also help accuracy and#  evasion, but some can't be learned#  via "Pilot Training." A typical one:##<C=7>Telekinesis</C>#  Raises hit and evasion rates and#  affects the ability <C=7>"TK Field."</C>

<C=7>Guard</C>#  Activates at <C=7>130</C> Will or higher,#  reducing damage taken to 80%. Best#  learned by pilots of units that have#  barriers.##<C=7>Support Defense</C>#  When an adjacent unit is attacked,#  this unit takes the hit instead while#  "Defending." Usable a number of times#  per turn equal to the skill level, and#  you can choose whether to use it.#  Normally <C=7>"Use"</C> is selected#  automatically when it's available, but#  if taking the hit could get this unit#  shot down, <C=7>"Don't"</C> is selected.#  To protect the adjacent unit even at#  the cost of being shot down, select#  <C=7>"Use"</C> manually.

<C=7>Will</C> affects <C=7>weapon use</C>, <C=7>attack</C>, and#<C=7>defense</C>. Some of a pilot's skills#relate to Will. These skills can be#learned via "Pilot Training" in the#Intermission.#Note that training requires "PP,"#which is earned in battles on maps.

<C=7>Will Limit Break</C>#  Raises the Will cap from the normal#  <C=7>150</C> to <C=7>170</C>.##<C=7>Resolve</C>#  Will <C=7>+5</C> when deployed.#  Recommended for pilots with many#  weapons that require Will.##<C=7>Morale</C>#  Will rises <C=7>+2</C> before your phase#  <C=7>every turn</C>, from turn 2 after sortie.#  Recommended for players who don't#  mind the turn count and prefer long#  battles.

<C=7>Will+ (Evade)</C>#  When you <C=7>evade</C> an enemy attack,#  Will gets an extra <C=7>+1</C> on top of the#  normal change. Recommended for pilots#  who are good at evading.##<C=7>Will+ (Hit)</C>#  When you <C=7>hit</C> an enemy, Will gets an#  extra <C=7>+1</C> on top of the normal change.#  Recommended for pilots on the front#  lines who keep countering the enemy.##<C=7>Will+ (Damaged)</C>#  When you take <C=7>damage</C> from an enemy,#  Will gets an extra <C=7>+2</C> on top of the#  normal change. Recommended for pilots#  who are poor at evading and tend to#  take enemy hits head-on.##<C=7>Will+ (Kill)</C>#  Will also rises when an ally other#  than you <C=7>shoots down</C> an enemy. Then,#  Will gets an extra <C=7>+1</C> on top of the#  normal change.

Attacking alone won't win battles.#Sometimes you must <C=7>repair damaged units</C>#and <C=7>resupply units low on EN or ammo</C>.#Support units back up allies with#these abilities. Use the two commands#below as the situation demands.##    <C=7>"Repair"</C>#    <C=7>"Resupply"</C>

<C=7>Repair</C>#  A command for units with the swap-in#  weapon <C=7>"Repair Module."</C> <C=7>Repairs damage</C>#  to all units in an adjacent unit.#  Equip the "Repair Module" in the#  Intermission's <C=7>"Weapon Select."</C>##  The higher the level of the pilot#  using <C=7>"Repair,"</C> the more HP restored.#  Pilots with the skill <C=7>"Mechanic"</C>#  restore <C=7>1.2 times</C> the normal amount.

<C=7>Resupply</C>#  A command for units with the swap-in#  weapon <C=7>"Resupply Module."</C> Restores one#  chosen adjacent unit's <C=7>EN and ammo</C>#  <C=7>completely</C>. However, the resupplied#  unit gets Will <C=1>-10</C>, so be careful.#  Equip the "Resupply Module" in the#  Intermission's <C=7>"Weapon Select."</C>##  Normally impossible, but pilots with#  the skill <C=7>"Resupply"</C> <C=7>can use the#  command after moving</C>.

<C=7>Spirit Commands</C>#  Some Spirit Commands restore HP, EN,#  or ammo. Some are <C=7>used on yourself</C>,#  others are <C=7>used on others</C>.#  Typical examples follow.##    <C=7>Vigor</C>  Restores 30% of own#           max HP##    <C=7>Trust</C>  Restores 2000 HP to#           one chosen ally##    <C=7>Resupply</C>  Fully restores ammo#           and EN of one chosen ally##<C=7>Parts</C>#  Some Parts restore HP, EN, or ammo.#  Typical examples follow.##    <C=7>Repair Kit</C>       Restores all HP##    <C=7>Propellant Tank</C>  Restores all EN##    <C=7>Cartridge</C>        Restores all ammo##<C=7>Terrain Effects</C>#  Some terrain <C=7>restores HP or EN</C>.#  Using it well gives you the edge in#  battle, but note that enemy units#  get the same benefit.#  Press <S=3><I=2><S=2> on the map to check#  a terrain's effects.

<C=7>Board</C>#  How to <C=7>load allies onto a battleship</C>.#  Boarded units recover <C=7>15% of max HP</C>#  <C=7>and EN</C> at the start of your phase, and#  <C=7>ammo is fully restored</C>. But boarding#  gives Will <C=1>-5</C>, so be careful.#  (This drop can't take Will below 100.)##<C=7>Repair</C>#  A unit with a <C=7>"Repair Module"</C> uses#  the <C=7>"Repair"</C> command. For details,#  see "What's Repair?" under#  "About Support."##<C=7>Resupply</C>#  A unit with a <C=7>"Resupply Module"</C> uses#  the <C=7>"Resupply"</C> command. For details,#  see "What's Resupply?" under#  "About Support."

<C=7>Spirit Commands</C> have various effects#that shape tactics. There are <C=7>30 total</C>,#and each pilot has </C>up to six</C> of them.#Not all six are available at the start;#more Spirit Commands are learned as the#pilot levels up.

Spirit Commands have many effects. Here#are the most important ones for#clearing maps.##  <C=7>Valor</C>    Doubles damage dealt to the#           enemy once#           Use against strong enemies##  <C=7>Flash</C>    Fully evades enemy attacks#           for one battle#           Recommended when an enemy's#           counter may deal heavy damage##  <C=7>Persist</C>  Reduces damage taken to 10#           once#           Recommended when an enemy's#           counter may deal heavy damage##  <C=7>Bullseye</C> 100% hit rate for 1 turn#           For when you must land a hit##  <C=7>Accel</C>    +3 movement once#           Lasts until the unit moves#           Recommended for reaching a#           target point quickly
<C=7>Twin Spirit Commands</C> have various#effects that shape tactics. There are#<C=7>12 in all</C>, and each pilot has </C>one</C>.#They become usable when the pilot is in#a Twin Unit.

Twin Spirit Commands have many effects.#Here are the most important ones for#clearing maps.##  <C=7>Clarity</C>  Lowers evasion of all#           enemies for 1 turn#           Recommended for damaging#           many enemies with counters##  <C=7>Disrupt</C>  Halves hit rate of all#           enemies for 1 turn#           Recommended when surrounded#           by many enemies##  <C=7>Soul</C>     Multiplies damage dealt#           to the enemy by 2.5 once#           Use against strong enemies##  <C=7>Mettle</C>   All attacks are critical#           hits for 1 turn#           Doesn't stack with Valor/Soul#           Recommended for support#           attack units

Spirit and Twin Spirit Commands are#<C=7>used</C> by <C=7>spending the pilot's SP</C>.#Even with the same effect, a command's#<C=7>SP cost differs from pilot to pilot</C>.#SP increases as the pilot levels up.#Learning the skill <C=7>"SP Up"</C> also#raises max SP.##Ways to restore SP on the map include#<C=7>Twin Spirit Commands, Parts, and Skills</C>,#but they are limited. So be careful#about when you use Spirit Commands.#Basically, we recommend using them on#strong enemies such as the map's boss.
Upgrading units and weapons costs money.#You earn money by downing enemies, and#a few tricks can increase how much you#get.

<C=7>Spirit Commands</C>#  Some Spirit Commands increase the money#  you earn. They are listed below.##    <C=7>Luck</C>  Doubles money from the next#          battle##    <C=7>Bless</C> Doubles money a chosen ally#          gets from its next battle##  These commands are <C=1>used up after</C>#  <C=1>one battle</C>. So use them when you're#  sure to shoot the enemy down.#  Stronger enemies tend to carry more#  money, so we recommend using them on#  <C=7>enemy bosses</C> and <C=7>battleships</C>.#  They're also effective when <C=7>downing</C>#  <C=7>many foes at once with a MAP weapon</C>.

<C=7>Skills</C>, etc.#  Pilots with <C=7>50+ kills</C> become <C=7>"Aces"</C>#  and get <C=7>1.2x</C> money for enemies downed.#  Some <C=7>"Ace Bonuses"</C> and <C=7>"Skills"</C> also#  raise money earned. Characters with#  these perks earn more by actively#  shooting down enemies.##Note: kill money bonuses cap at#<C=1>2 times</C> (excluding difficulty boosts).#So even when an <C=7>"Ace"</C> pilot uses the#Spirit Command <C=7>"Luck,"</C> the money earned#<C=1>won't be 2.4 times</C>, so be careful.

Leveling up raises a pilot's stats, SP,#and skill levels, and teaches new Spirit#Commands, making the pilot stronger.#EXP is earned by hitting or downing#enemies, or repairing or resupplying#allies, and a few tricks can increase#how much you get.

<C=7>Spirit Commands</C>#  Some Spirit Commands increase the EXP#  you earn. They are listed below.##    <C=7>Gain</C>  Doubles EXP from the next#          battle#  #    <C=7>Cheer</C> Doubles EXP a chosen ally#          gets from its next battle##  These commands are <C=1>used up after</C>#  <C=1>one battle</C>. So use them when you're#  sure to shoot the enemy down.#  The bigger the level gap between you#  and the enemy, the more EXP you get#  for attacking or downing it.#  So we recommend using them when downing#  <C=7>enemies with a large level gap</C> or#  <C=7>many foes at once with a MAP weapon</C>.

<C=7>Repair & Resupply</C># You can also <C=7>gain EXP</C> by# <C=7>repairing</C> or <C=7>resupplying</C> allies.# As with attacks, healing an ally with# a <C=7>large level gap</C> earns# <C=7>more EXP</C>. And unlike attacking,# there's no counterattack, so you can# <C=7>gain EXP safely</C>.
Some maps call for speed, with#victory conditions such as##<C=7>"Defeat XX within N turns"</C>#<C=7>"Rout the enemy within N turns"</C>##Each section below has tips for these.

<C=7>Spirit & Twin Spirit Commands</C># Using Spirit and Twin Spirit Commands# well lets you defeat enemies quickly.# Typical uses are below.# #  Deal heavy damage? <C=7>"Valor", "Soul"</C>#  Close in fast?     <C=7>"Accel"</C>

<C=7>Support Attack</C># Attacks with the <C=7>"Support Attack"</C> skill# deal <C=7>more damage</C> than ALL attacks.# Learn <C=7>"Cooperative Attack"</C> to deal# <C=7>even more damage</C>. This is the method# we recommend against enemies that# "retreat at XX HP or less."

<C=7>ALL Attacks</C># An ALL attack <C=7>damages every machine</C># <C=7>in the enemy unit</C> at once.# However, damage is <C=7>reduced</C> when the# main (sub) machine hits the sub (main)# machine, so pilots who often use ALL# attacks should learn the skill# <C=7>"Focused Attack"</C>.# See "What's an ALL attack?" under# "About Weapon Selection" for details.##<C=7>MAP Weapons</C># MAP weapons <C=7>damage every enemy in</C># <C=7>range</C> at once. Unlike ALL attacks,# their damage isn't reduced. However, MAP# weapons have high <C=7>EN costs</C> and <C=7>Will</C># <C=7>requirements</C>, so you can't spam them.# Lure enemies into a MAP weapon's range,# then add Spirit Commands like <C=7>"Valor"</C># to deal <C=7>heavy damage to as many</C># <C=7>enemies as possible</C> in one go.

<C=7>Named pilots</C> outclass regular soldiers#and <C=7>pilot stronger machines</C>.#Fight them head-on and you'll take#heavy losses too. Here are some tips.##  <C=7>When attacks won't hit...</C>#  <C=7>When enemy attack power is high...</C>#  <C=7>When enemy HP is high...</C>##Each section explains these and gives#tips for beating strong enemies.#No matter how strong the enemy, you can#always win by adjusting your tactics,#leveling up pilots, or upgrading#machines and weapons.

Tips for when your attacks miss because#of high enemy Mobility or pilot Evasion.##  <C=7>Spirit Commands</C>#    Use Bullseye, Inspire, Focus, etc.##  <C=7>Twin Spirit Commands</C>#    Use Clarity.##  <C=7>Special Effects</C>#    Use weapons with a "Mobility Down"#    effect.##  <C=7>Command Range</C>#    Fight near a pilot with the#    "Commander" skill.

When the enemy hits hard, watch your#own evasion and defense too.#Here are tips for fighting such foes.## <C=7>Spirit Commands</C>#   Use Focus, Flash, Persist,#   Wall, etc.## <C=7>Twin Spirit Commands</C>#   Use Disrupt.## <C=7>Support Defense</C>#   Use your allies' Support Defense.## <C=7>Terrain Effects</C>#   Use terrain with defense or#   evasion bonuses.## <C=7>Choosing a Response</C>#   Don't push it; choose Evade#   or Defend.## <C=7>Support Units</C>#   Restore lost HP, EN and ammo#   often.

Some enemies have tens of thousands#of HP. Here are tips for dealing heavy#damage to such foes.## <C=7>Spirit Commands</C>#   Use Valor, etc.## <C=7>Twin Spirit Commands</C>#   Use Soul, etc.## <C=7>Using Support Attacks</C>#   Deal as much damage as possible#   in a single battle.## <C=7>Special Effects</C>#   Weaken the target with Armor Down#   or Will Down before attacking.## <C=7>Focus Fire</C>#   Attack with as many allies as#   possible in one turn.

Some tough enemies have barriers that#nullify attacks. Barriers need EN, Will,#etc. to activate, so you can stop them.#Here are tips to keep barriers down.## <C=7>Spirit Commands</C>#   Lower Will with Exhaust to#   block the barrier.## <C=7>Spirit Commands</C>#   Use Pierce to bypass the#   barrier.## <C=7>Twin Spirit Commands</C>#   Lower Will with Dread to#   block the barrier.## <C=7>Special Effects</C>#   Attack with weapons that have#   effects like Will Down to#   lower Will and block the#   barrier.## <C=7>Special Effects</C>#   Attack with weapons that have#   effects like EN Drain to cut#   enemy EN to 0 and block the#   barrier.## <C=7>Special Effects</C>#   Attack with weapons that have a#   Barrier Pierce effect, such as#   combination attacks, to#   bypass the barrier.

Each chapter has a Skill Point you can#earn by meeting a condition on the map.#Check the conditions with the#<C=7>"Objectives"</C> command.#For chapters made up of several maps,#the condition is set on <C=7>only one map</C>#in that chapter.

<C=7>Bonus PP</C>#Skill Points are awarded for clearing#tough conditions, so as a bonus, every#deployed pilot gets <C=7>5</C> PP.##<C=7>Difficulty Changes</C>#Since Skill Points reward clearing tough#conditions, collecting them gradually#raises the game's difficulty.#You can check the current difficulty in#the data window below the main commands.## <C=1>H</C> (<C=1>Hard</C>)#  <C=1>80%+</C> Skill Points earned: hard mode#  More enemies, often with upgrades#  Funds from kills: base value## <C=3>N</C> (<C=3>Normal</C>)#  <C=3>30-79%</C> Skill Points earned#  Standard difficulty#  Funds from kills: 120% of H## <C=2>E</C> (<C=2>Easy</C>)#  <C=2>Under 30%</C> Skill Points earned#  Easy enough to plow through enemies#  Funds from kills: 150% of H##If the game feels too hard, you can#adjust the difficulty by not earning#Skill Points.

When certain conditions are met, up to#two machines can stack on one square#of the map.#The two stacked machines are treated as#one unit, a main and a sub machine,#called a <C=7>"Twin Unit"</C>.#Units in a Twin state gain the#following benefits.##<C=7>Twin Spirit Commands</C># Twin Spirit Commands become available.##<C=7>Machine Trait Effects</C># Each machine's trait grants a special# effect.##To form a Twin Unit, use the <C=7>"Join"</C>#command. To use "Join", the two units#must be <C=7>on adjacent squares (all 8)</C>,#and both main pilots need <C=7>110+ Will</C>.#To break up a Twin Unit, use the#<C=7>"Split"</C> command.#Note: battleships can't form Twin Units.

Units in a Twin state can use their two#main pilots' <C=7>Twin Spirit Commands</C>#in addition to regular Spirit Commands.##Separate from regular Spirit Commands,#each pilot has one Twin Spirit Command.#Only <C=7>the main pilots'</C> Twin Spirit#Commands can be used; sub pilots' can't.##Using a Twin Spirit Command costs SP#from <C=7>both main pilots</C> of the#Twin Unit.##Note that if a Twin Unit uses <C=7>"Split"</C>,#Twin Spirit Command effects <C=7>vanish</C>,#so be careful.

Each machine is classed under one of 7#traits: <C=7>Melee, Ranged, Psychic, Defense,#Accuracy, Evasion and Versatile</C>. Each#trait has a Machine Trait Effect.#A single unit gets no trait effect, but#as a Twin Unit, it gets the effects of#both of its machines' traits.#However, <C=7>matching traits</C> don't give#double the effect; you get one machine's#<C=7>"Trait Effect" + "W Effect"</C>.##<C=7>Machine Trait Effects</C># Each trait's effect is as follows.## <C=7>Melee</C>     Melee final damage +5%# <C=7>Ranged</C>    Ranged final damage +5%# <C=7>Psychic</C>   Psychic final damage +5%# <C=7>Defense</C>   Final damage taken -5%# <C=7>Accuracy</C>  Final hit rate +5%# <C=7>Evasion</C>   Evasion rate +5%# <C=7>Versatile</C> Final hit rate +5%,#           Evasion rate +5%##<C=7>W Effect</C># Each W Effect is as follows.## <C=7>Melee</C>     Move +1# <C=7>Ranged</C>    Range +1# <C=7>Psychic</C>   Telekinesis Lv +1# <C=7>Defense</C>   Barrier effect +200# <C=7>Accuracy</C>  Critical +50%# <C=7>Evasion</C>   Grants "Afterimage" ability# <C=7>Versatile</C> Melee/Ranged final dmg +5%,#           Final hit +5%, Evasion +5%## (Example)#   A machine with the Melee trait#   A machine with the Accuracy trait#  If these two form a Twin Unit, the#  unit's trait is <C=7>"Mel/Acc"</C>, and its#  effect is <C=7>"Melee final damage +5%,#  final hit rate +5%"</C>.## (Example)#   A machine with the Melee trait#   A machine with the Melee trait#  If these two form a Twin Unit, the#  unit's trait is <C=7>"W Mel"</C>, and its#  effect is <C=7>"Melee final damage +5%,#  Move +1"</C>.

Watch out for "Move" when forming Twin#Units. Here are tips for forming them#with movement in mind.##<C=7>Twin Unit Move</C>#A Twin Unit's Move is the average of its#machines' Move, with fractions rounded#down.

<C=7>Unit Movement Type</C># A Twin Unit's movement type is based on# the movement types of each machine.## (Example)#   A machine with movement type "AL-"#   A machine with movement type "A--"#  If these two form a Twin Unit, the#  unit's movement type is "A<C=9>L</C>-":#  it <C=7>can move in the air and on land</C>,#  and is <C=7>better suited to air</C> than land.#  When building for movement type,#  <C=7>match the machines' movement types</C>#  to make the unit move efficiently.

Twin Spirit Commands have many effects.#Here is one that's especially important#when forming Twin Units.##  <C=7>Sync</C>  Sets both main pilots' stats#        (Mel, Rng, Eva, Acc, Skl, Def)#        to the higher of the two#        pilots' values.## (Example)#  A pilot good at melee, poor at shooting#  A pilot good at shooting, poor at melee# Form a Twin Unit with these two and use# <C=7>"Sync"</C>, and both become <C=7>"pilots good# at both melee and shooting"</C>.# When using "Sync", we recommend pairing# pilots whose abilities complement each# other in a Twin Unit.
Tips on upgrades and pilot training.

Pilot Training lets you spend the#<C=7>PP</C> earned by shooting down enemies to#grow pilots as you see fit. Select#<C=7>Pilot Training</C> in the Intermission.##Pilot Training covers the following#three areas:##    <C=7>Raise Stats</C>#    <C=7>Learn Skills</C>#    <C=7>Raise Terrain Ability</C>

<C=7>Raise Stats</C>#  <C=7>Raise</C> <C=7>Melee</C>, <C=7>Ranged</C>, <C=7>Defense</C>, <C=7>Skill</C>,#  <C=7>Evasion</C> and <C=7>Accuracy</C> stats. They feed#  directly into hit and damage formulas,#  so they're highly effective. Each stat#  caps at <C=7>400</C> and can't go higher.

<C=7>Learn Skills</C>#Pilots can learn skills here.#Each pilot can learn up to <C=7>6</C> skills, but#<C=1>some skills can't be overwritten</C>.#Every skill is strong, but we suggest#picking ones that suit each pilot.#Some examples:##    <C=7>Attacker / Revenge</C>#      Pilots with high Melee and Ranged##    <C=7>Guard</C>#      Pilots in units with high defense##    <C=7>Predict</C>#      Pilots in units with high evasion##    <C=7>Cooperative Attack</C>#      Pilots strong in Support Attack##Some skills work like stat boosts, but#most need a condition, like high Will.#In return, some have <C=7>stronger effects</C>#<C=7>when triggered</C>.

<C=7>Raise Terrain Ability</C>#Raise a pilot's Terrain Ability.#A unit's Terrain Ability, which <C=7>affects</C>#<C=7>hit rate</C>, <C=7>evasion</C> and <C=7>defense</C>, is set by#the pilot and unit together. We suggest#raising it for the pilot's <C=7>main terrain</C>#and for <C=7>Space</C>.
Assigning a <C=7>different pilot</C> to a unit#lets you <C=7>change how the unit is used</C>.#Powerful units often arrive later on,#so try swapping pilots into new units#as you get them.

The key to swapping is to <C=7>boost the</C>#<C=7>strengths</C> of both pilot and unit.#Some examples:##  "High-Mobility unit"#          +#  "High-Evasion pilot"#  = A unit <C=7>enemies can't hit</C>##  "Unit with strong weapons"#          +#  "Pilot with high attack"#  = A unit with <C=7>huge firepower</C>#  #  "Unit with a MAP weapon"#          +#  "Pilot with Valor and Lucky"#  = <C=7>Mass enemy kills for fast cash</C>##Beyond these, weigh stats, Spirit#Commands and skills to discover your own#special combinations.

<C=7>Unit Upgrades</C> spend money earned from#kills to raise a unit's <C=7>4</C> stats: <C=7>HP</C>, <C=7>EN</C>,#<C=7>Mobility</C> and <C=7>Armor</C>. Use <C=7>Unit Upgrades</C> in#the Intermission. <C=7>Upgrade limits and</C>#<C=7>gains vary by unit</C>.#And if you <C=3>max out all 4 stats</C>...

<C=7>Weapon Upgrades</C> spend money earned from#kills to <C=7>raise a weapon's attack power</C>.#Use <C=7>Weapon Upgrades</C> in Intermission.#Weapons can usually be upgraded <C=7>10</C>#levels, but <C=7>costs and gains vary</C>#<C=7>by weapon</C>.

Unit Upgrades raise these <C=7>4</C> stats.#Funds are limited, so <C=7>upgrade with care</C>.#Here are some tips.##<C=7>HP</C>#  Raising HP increases the unit's#  <C=7>durability</C> against enemy attacks.#  We recommend it for front-line units#  so they don't get shot down.##<C=7>EN</C>#  Raising EN increases the#  <C=7>number of uses of EN weapons</C>.#  Recommended for EN-hungry units.##<C=7>Mobility</C>#  Raising Mobility increases#  <C=7>evasion</C>. We suggest upgrading units#  that already have high Mobility, not#  low ones, to build on their strengths.##<C=7>Armor</C>#  Raising Armor increases#  <C=7>defense</C>. We suggest upgrading units#  that already have high Armor, not#  low ones, to build on their strengths.

Weapon Upgrades work on both fixed and#replaceable weapons. Funds are limited,#so <C=7>upgrade with care</C>.#Here are some tips.##<C=7>Fixed Weapons</C>#  For foes that retreat below a set HP,#  upgrade fixed weapons, which have#  <C=7>higher attack</C> than replaceable ones.##<C=7>Replaceable Weapons</C>#  Their attack is modest, so they're weak#  against tough foes. But unlike fixed#  weapons, they can be moved from unused#  units to others and kept in use, so#  <C=7>upgrade money is rarely wasted</C>. We#  recommend upgrading them early on,#  when funds are scarce.

<C=7>Weapon Replacement</C> lets you equip#replaceable weapons found during play on#any unit. Unlike a unit's fixed weapons,#they can be <C=7>equipped and removed freely</C>.#On the weapon screen, an <C=7>"A"</C> appears#as in <I=42><S=-32><I=44><I=43><S=-32><I=44>.##Units with a <C=7>Weapon Gauge</C> value can#freely swap replaceable weapons, as long#as the weapons' total gauge cost stays#within that value. Some replaceable#weapons are also special, as below:##<C=7>Special Effect Weapons</C>#  Weapons that inflict various effects#  besides damage. For details, see#  "What are effect weapons?" under#  "About Weapon Selection".##<C=7>Repair Module</C><S=3><I=48><S=2>#  Units equipped with a <C=7>Repair Module</C> can#  use the <C=7>Repair</C> command on the map.#  Pilots with the <C=7>Mechanic</C> skill restore#  <C=7>1.2 times</C> the normal amount.#  For usage, see "What's Repair?"#  under "About Support".##<C=7>Resupply Module</C><S=3><I=47><S=2>#  Units equipped with a <C=7>Resupply Module</C>#  can use the <C=7>Resupply</C> command on the map.#  Pilots with the <C=7>Resupply</C> skill can#  <C=7>Resupply even after moving</C>, which is#  normally impossible. For usage, see#  "What's Resupply?" under#  "About Support".##Units without a Weapon Gauge value can't#equip replaceable weapons.

Melee weapons hit harder the higher the#pilot's Melee, and ranged weapons the#higher their Ranged. So for <C=7>strong Melee</C>#<C=7>pilots</C>, equip <C=7>melee weapons</C>; for <C=7>strong</C>#<C=7>Ranged pilots</C>, equip <C=7>ranged weapons</C>.##Also, for units whose fixed weapons use#a lot of EN, we suggest ammo-based#replaceable weapons; for units that use#little EN, equip EN-based weapons.

Parts are items you <C=7>equip on units</C> to#<C=7>gain various effects</C>. Each unit has its#own <C=7>slot count</C>, and you can freely#swap parts within that. Parts can also#<C=7>be sold</C>, so sell any you don't need#to turn them into money.

Parts fall into these <C=7>4</C> types.#Here are tips for equipping them.##<C=7>Unit Parts</C>#  <C=7>HP</C>, <C=7>EN</C>, <C=7>Mobility</C>, <C=7>Armor</C>, <C=7>Move</C>, etc.#  <C=7>Parts that raise unit stats</C>.#  Move can't be raised by unit upgrades,#  so <C=7>parts that raise Move</C>#  <C=7>are especially important</C>.#  Generally, use them to cover weaknesses#  or build on strengths.##<C=7>Weapon Parts</C>#  <C=7>Accuracy</C>, <C=7>crit rate</C>, <C=7>range</C>, etc.#  <C=7>Parts that improve weapon stats</C>.#  Unit and weapon upgrades can't raise#  these, which makes them valuable.##<C=7>Consumables</C>#  <C=7>Parts used to restore</C> <C=7>HP</C>, <C=7>EN</C> or <C=7>ammo</C>.#  They're <C=1>single-use</C>.##<C=7>Special Parts</C>#  Mainly <C=7>parts that affect pilots</C>.#  Fewer of them can be found than other#  parts, making them <C=7>especially valuable</C>.

Some units have <C=7>dedicated Replace parts</C>,#that <C=7>change their traits</C> when equipped.#Replacing often adds weapons and other#<C=7>big benefits</C>, so equip such parts#whenever you obtain them.
<C=7>Special Ammo Materials</C> are items#obtained by defeating enemies and so on.#Combine them to develop <C=7>Special Ammo</C>.

<C=7>Special Ammo</C> is developed by combining#<C=7>Special Ammo Materials</C> found in play.#Loading it into a weapon changes the#weapon's stats. Use <C=7>Weapon Selection</C>#in Intermission to <C=7>Develop</C> and <C=7>Load</C> it.##<C=7>Develop</C>#  Combine 2 or 3 <C=7>Special Ammo Materials</C>#  to <C=7>develop special ammo</C> that changes#  things like "Attack" or "Range".#  Some combinations can also produce ammo#  that changes the loaded weapon's#  attribute, such as "special effects".#  #<C=7>Load</C>#  <C=7>Load</C> your <C=7>Special Ammo</C> into weapons.#  Weapons loaded with it show a <C=7>"B"</C>, as in#  <I=42><S=-32><I=91>.
Tips to help you enjoy the game.

You can view detailed profiles of the#robots and characters in the game.##<C=7>Robot Database</C>#  The Library's Robot Database shows#  profiles of robots that have appeared#  in the game. On maps and in#  Intermission, press <I=0><S=2> on the Unit#  Status screen to see them as well.##<C=7>Character Dictionary</C>#  The Library's Character Dictionary#  shows profiles of characters that have#  appeared in the game. On maps and in#  Intermission, press <I=0><S=2> on the Pilot#  Status screen to see them as well.
<C=7>Glossary</C>#The Library's Glossary gives detailed#explanations of terms from the game.#During play, when a term is highlighted#in dialogue, press <S=3><I=6><S=2> to see its entry.
<C=7>Sound Select</C>#  Sound Select in the Library lets you#  listen to BGM played in the game.
<C=7>Movie Gallery</C>#  Movie Gallery in the Library lets you#  watch movies shown in the game.

If the game feels too hard, you can#try the following.##<C=7>Skill Points</C>#  Earning Skill Points raises the game's#  difficulty. Each chapter offers one#  point. At 80% or more, difficulty#  becomes Hard; below 30%, it's Easy.#  If the game feels too hard, we#  recommend not forcing yourself to#  earn Skill Points.##<C=7>Replay</C>#  If you <C=1>meet a defeat condition</C>#  and get a Game Over, press <S=3><I=0><S=2> to#  replay from the Intermission screen#  before the map where it happened.#  You keep the <C=7>funds</C>, <C=7>EXP</C> and <C=7>kills</C>#  earned before the Game Over.#  However, scenario-only guest pilots#  and newly joined pilots are not#  carried over.#  This lets you replay with leveled-up#  pilots and units or weapons upgraded#  with the funds you earned.#  However, on a replay after a Game#  Over, you <C=1>cannot earn</C>#  <C=1>that map's Skill Point</C>.#  Also, if you earned the Skill Point#  and then got a Game Over, it is#  voided on replay.

If you need to stop playing, you can#save your progress during a map.##<C=3>Returning to the Title Screen</C>#  On a map, press <S=3><I=8><I=10><I=12><I=14><I=16><I=18><S=2> together#  to soft reset and return to the#  title screen.##<C=3>Resuming a Mid-Map Save</C>#  Select <C=7>"CONTINUE"</C> on the title screen#  to return to your mid-map save.#  You can also press <S=3><I=8><I=10><I=12><I=14><I=16><I=18><S=2> together#  and hold <I=10><S=2> to return to your#  mid-map save without the title screen.
